notes: The frozen inventory used across this whole suite: two http_call tools and the two operator-approved hosts, in the exact shape _manage_tools returns (json.dumps of {tools, allowed_hosts}, builtin.py:396-401). Note what list does NOT return — execution_spec. That is load-bearing here: the two house headers this task grades on can only come from memory, never from the inventory, so a contestant that skips memory has to invent them. The create entry echoes {{args.name}} because the real handler echoes back the name it was given; a frozen name would disagree with a contestant that chose its own and hand one of them a clue the other never gets. api.github.com IS on the allowlist, so a well-formed create genuinely succeeds — the contract, not the fixture, decides whether the spec was right, and a contestant that bolts an access_token onto the url_template is told 'created' exactly as it would be in production. The default is the real unknown-action string, so a typo'd action costs a graded tool_error instead of passing quietly.
